name: GlutenScanner: gluten free
description:
Scan the barcode and see instantly whether a product contains gluten.

GlutenScanner is made for anyone living gluten-free - with coeliac disease, gluten intolerance, or by choice. Instead of squinting at the small print, you get a clear answer: red, yellow or green.

HOW IT WORKS
Scan the barcode with your camera, or type it in. You get the answer right away and can see the full ingredient list with gluten sources highlighted. If a product is not in the database, photograph the ingredient list - the text is read on your own phone.

TRAVEL CARD
Travelling abroad? Show the staff a clear message about coeliac disease in their own language. The travel card covers 18 languages - from French, Italian and Spanish to Greek, Polish, Turkish, Chinese, Thai and Japanese - grouped by situation: the short main message, questions about the menu, questions about a specific dish, and questions about cross-contamination in the kitchen. Made for use in both shops and restaurants.

MORE THAN GLUTEN
Besides gluten, 14 other allergens are flagged, including milk, nuts, peanuts, soy and egg. The app also checks maltodextrin separately: is it made from wheat, or from a gluten-free source such as maize or potato?

MAKE IT YOURS
Choose which allergens are highlighted in the result. If you are sensitive to oats, switch on an extra warning so gluten-free oats show as red instead of yellow. Switch between a light and dark look, or let the app follow your phone.

WORKS WITHOUT INTERNET
Every scan is saved to your history and can be looked up again instantly - even standing in a shop with no signal. Star the products you buy often to keep them at the top.

YOUR PRIVACY
No user accounts. No ads. No tracking. Your scan history stays on your own phone and is never sent to us. Ingredient lists in other languages are translated locally on your device.

IN YOUR LANGUAGE
Available in Danish, English, German, Spanish, Swedish and Norwegian, and picks the language from your phone automatically.

HELP OTHERS
If a product is missing, you can submit it with three photos. It is reviewed manually and added for the benefit of everyone else.

IMPORTANT
GlutenScanner is a helper tool, not medical advice. Assessments are based on product databases and automated lookups that may be incomplete or outdated. Always read the ingredient list on the packaging yourself - especially with coeliac disease or severe gluten intolerance.

Some product data comes from Open Food Facts and is used under the Open Database License (ODbL).

name: How to Gluten Free
description:
How to Gluten Free helps coeliacs eat away from home: the places we checked, a trip planner, a label tool and a meal planner, with the same evidence rule under each.

ONE PERSON, NOT FOUR CATEGORIES
Whether you are travelling, packing a lunchbox, cooking or reading a label, you are the same coeliac. One site, one app, one community. Four tools, one person:

EAT OUT: Atlas, the places we checked
14,000+ gluten-free places in 90+ countries, on a map that never flattens the difference: gold ★ for verified dedicated kitchens, a separate marker for self-declared places awaiting our check, GF-serving from shared kitchens. Every listing carries a dated evidence line: the source we relied on and the date we last checked it. Filter by what a coeliac actually asks: Dedicated fryer · Separate prep · Staff trained · GF menu. Recall alerts for the countries you choose. Stadiums, theme parks, hospitals: the venue types few maps bother with.

PLAN: Compass, your trip and route planner (beta)
Build a trip stop by stop and see the listed places along the way: at both airports, around the midpoint, on every stretch. A scouting aid for the week before, not road navigation.

LEARN: Label Lab and the field guide
Label Lab tells you what a gluten-free claim, a logo or a "may contain" line means on a label: pick your market: EU, UK, USA, Canada or Australia/New Zealand. Translation cards show staff what you need, in their language, written for coeliacs, not for tourists. The Ingredient Decoder reads an ingredient list with you, the Translator carries coeliac questions to the table, and the Flour Library explains every gluten-free flour and what it stands in for.

COOK: Meal Lab (beta)
A week planner with a grocery list: plan the week, shop once. New, and growing.

WHAT "DEDICATED" AND "VERIFIED BY US" MEAN
★ Dedicated marks a kitchen that is 100% gluten-free: nothing containing gluten is prepared there, so there is no shared fryer, oven or prep bench to worry about. "Verified by us" means we checked the evidence; a review never earns it. A place that calls itself dedicated but hasn't been through our check is shown as "Dedicated claim, pending our check", clearly and without the star. Community reports are read by us before they appear; they are experience, never a safety verdict, and they never set a tier.

HELP US MAP IT
Found a dedicated bakery we don't have yet? Somewhere that closed, or changed its protocol? Tap "Suggest a place" or "Report a change": three taps, straight to our review team, and we check every single one. A map of real places is never finished: it gets better every week, and your finds are part of that.

SAFETY INFORMATION IS NEVER BEHIND A PAYWALL
Tiers, the evidence line, search, the map, Label Lab, the translation cards and recall alerts are free for everyone, with no account needed, and they stay free. Any optional membership only ever unlocks travel conveniences such as offline packs and trip boards, never the evidence.

A NOTE ON TRUST
How to Gluten Free is a travel and communication aid, not a medical service, and not a guarantee. Always confirm the gluten-free protocol with staff when you arrive.

name: Food Recall & Allergy Alerts
description:
Food Recall & Allergy Alerts — Know when a UK food alert names something you eat.

Food recall warnings and allergy alerts matter while the pack is still in your fridge. The Food Standards Agency publishes them as open data; this app checks them for the foods, brands and allergens you name.

This app is NOT affiliated with the FSA and is NOT medical advice. An alert covers particular packs, batches or use-by dates, and only the label on your own pack says whether it is inside one — treat a match as “go and read the official notice”. If you have a food allergy, act on the FSA notice, not on this app.

WHAT IT DOES
• Matching reads the title, product, business AND declared allergen list — 23 of 256 FSA alerts from Jan 2025 to Sep 2026 had an allergen missing from title and product
• Watch a food, a brand or an allergen — or leave the box EMPTY and watch every UK food alert
• Your word never leaves the phone — matching happens on the device
• Filter to allergy alerts only, product recalls only, or both
• No match does not mean a food is safe — always read the label

HOW YOU SET IT UP
You create one watch — for example “mustard, gluten or a supermarket name” — and close the app. At the interval you choose it checks food recalls and allergy alerts published by the FSA; when the FSA publishes a food alert matching your watch your phone gets a notification. It never tells you about the same thing twice. If checking breaks (server down, page changed) it says so instead of dying quietly. Settings shows how many bytes each check costs. Light and dark theme.

WHO IT IS FOR
Anyone with a food allergy or intolerance, and their carers.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
• It does NOT give medical or dietary advice and is no substitute for reading a label. A quiet week never means a food is safe — an alert exists only once a business reports a problem.
• It does NOT arrange the refund; that is claimed from the business in the notice.
• It does NOT sign in and never asks for personal details.
• It asks you for no account. No sign-up, no password.
• No personal data goes to the developer. Google's ad SDK collects IP, interactions, diagnostics and device IDs.
• The free tier is paid for by ads: banner, interstitial, rewarded, rewarded interstitial, app open, and an “Ad”-labelled card in your watch list. No interstitial on launch; a rewarded interstitial always opens with an intro screen you can skip. Paid members see none of them and no ad request is sent.
• Nothing of it stays pinned to your notification shade.

WHAT IT COVERS
Every food alert the FSA publishes — product recalls (PRIN) and allergy alerts (AA) — 17 in a typical sixty-day window, and each check reads that whole window so a phone that was off still catches up.

THE ALLERGEN LIST IS STRUCTURED, NOT GUESSED
Each alert carries its declared allergens as named values — Gluten, Mustard, Milk — and the app reads that list directly, so watching “mustard” finds an alert whose headline never says it.

PRIVACY
The foods and allergens you follow are stored on the device and nowhere else — the developer operates no server to receive them. Permissions requested: network state, internet, notifications, letting the ads library tell Wi-Fi from mobile data, restarting watches after a reboot, vibration, keeping the phone awake while a check runs, buying a paid membership through Google Play and ads in the free tier.

LIMITS — honestly
• Android may delay background checks to save battery. The interval you pick is a target, not a guarantee.
• Very frequent checking is deliberately limited out of respect for the FSA food alerts list.

name: NutriSpy: Food & Symptom Diary
description:
NutriSpy is a food diary that finds your patterns. A symptom that keeps coming back, a bad gut day, an afternoon with no energy — and no idea what caused it. Log what you eat, how you slept and how you feel, and NutriSpy puts it all on one timeline and shows you what goes with your worse days. Verifiable from week one, in your own days.

Make sense of your symptoms

Complaints often trail their trigger by hours, so memory alone rarely finds the connection. NutriSpy records meals and symptoms with their times and shows which habits and foods go with your better and worse days — more fat in the evening, a shorter night, fewer steps — what settles your digestion, and what leaves you drained. It is honest about how strong each pattern is — a hunch is labelled a hunch.

A food diary that fits your life

Log meals, symptoms, bowel movements, sleep, activity and supplements by voice, photo, barcode or text — one sentence is enough, NutriSpy structures it. Sleep and workouts sync from Apple Health or Health Connect, so your diary fills itself while you live your day.

See what actually helps you

Whether you want to calm your digestion, get to the bottom of a symptom, have more energy or sleep better, NutriSpy shows which foods and habits help and which hold you back. Your daily form tells you at a glance how the day is going, and a coach tip tells you what to try next. Want to lose weight or build muscle instead? Calories, protein and your weight trend sit side by side, with a calorie target that follows your goal. Full nutrient data sits underneath: calories, macros, fiber, vitamins, minerals, omega-3/6 and supplements. Fiber is counted under every meal, soluble and insoluble separately.

See your patterns

NutriSpy connects nutrition, digestion, symptoms, sleep, activity and cycle, and highlights the relationships that matter for you — "your bloating tends to follow high-fat evenings", not generic averages. A bowel movement or a symptom takes seconds to log and becomes part of the picture instead of another chore.

No pressure to be perfect

You don't have to log everything, every day. Miss a day and your insights still work — this food diary is built for real life, not streaks. Share your log with your doctor or coach whenever it helps.

Free food diary, Premium insights

The food diary is free, AI logging included: meals, symptoms, bowel movements, sleep and supplements by voice, photo or text, with calories and macros. Premium adds the insights: which foods and habits go with your symptoms, the full nutrient and FODMAP analysis with lactose, fructose and the polyols, six months of sleep trends, a coach tip on every entry, sync back to your health app, and a CSV or PDF report for your doctor. For IBS, food intolerance, histamine or heartburn, that makes your food log a symptom tracker. Prices in the app.

Important: NutriSpy is not a diagnostic tool and should not be used for medical diagnoses, treatments, or as a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult qualified healthcare professionals for health concerns or medical decisions.
